grid.$description: Data cells and the sheet grid. A grid has corners.

chip.$description: Traits and rank pips, small and stamped.

control.$description: Buttons and fields. Softer than a chip, tighter than a panel, so a control never reads as a card.

sheet.$description: Bottom sheets, which meet the screen edge.

min.$description: Absolute floor. Nothing interactive is smaller.

default.$description: Standard control height on a phone.

separation.$description: Minimum gap between two adjacent tap targets so a mis-tap needs real travel.

control.$description: Sizes that change with the pointer in use. The hit box is always tap.min; only the drawn mark and the track shrink, so a fine pointer gets a precise mark without the target ever going under the floor.

thumb-coarse.$description: Slider thumb mark under a finger. Equal to the tap floor, because here the mark is the target.

thumb-fine.$description: Slider thumb mark under a mouse. Small enough to point at a single value on a twenty-step scale.

track-coarse.$description: Slider track under a finger. Thick enough to aim at when the thumb is under the fingertip.

viewport-min.$description: Smallest phone we lay out for.

viewport-target.$description: Design width. A player at a table is on a phone, so this is where the layout is decided; design/003 added the two widths below for everyone else.

viewport-wide.$description: A tablet, or a phone turned sideways. Grids of short labels gain a second column here; prose does not.

viewport-desk.$description: A laptop. Navigation stands up as a rail beside the content and a record opens next to the list rather than over it. A media query cannot read a custom property, so this value is repeated literally in every query that uses it; this is where it is decided.

content-max.$description: Caps line length when a large phone or tablet is used. Around 65 characters at the body size, which is the measure prose keeps at any viewport.

bottom-bar.$description: Primary navigation sits in the thumb arc, not the top of the screen.

rail.$description: The bar stood up beside the content on a laptop. Wider than the bar is thick, because a label under an icon needs room a thumb target does not.

thumb-reach.$description: Fraction of viewport height from the bottom that a thumb covers one-handed. Primary actions live inside it.

safe-bottom.$description: Height of the home indicator strip. A token rather than the raw function so every bottom-edge surface reserves the same room and one grep finds them all.

hair.$description: Separation is a border, not a shadow. Shadows are only for things that genuinely float.
